title: EventEnvelope
description:
Events are a durable stream with consumer groups, at-least-once delivery and ordering within a session partition - not fire-and-forget pub/sub, which silently drops recording.completed when a consumer is down. The envelope is the second of exactly two contact points between the Go and Python halves.

Payloads are typed per event type through the allOf below. Only the events the platform currently emits are typed; the rest keep an open payload deliberately, because inventing a shape for an event no code produces yet is how a data model gets locked wrong. THE RULE: an event type must have a payload schema in this file before any code emits it. An open payload does not generate a type - it generates map[string]any, dict and Record<string, unknown> - so an event left open is an event with no SDK contract.

eventId.description: Doubles as the idempotency key for webhook delivery. 128 bits, because consumers store these and the width cannot be changed after issue.

version.description: Per-event version. Additive by default; behaviour never changes silently.

sequence.description: Monotonic within the session partition. Ordering is guaranteed here and nowhere else.

occurredAt.description: RFC 3339 with a UTC offset and millisecond precision. The pattern is asserted alongside the format because format assertion is opt-in in most validators, so a format keyword alone would be documentation rather than a check.

traceId.description: W3C trace id. One trace per turn, not per session.

EventType.description: agent.state_changed is the most important event for user experience: a user who can see 'thinking' waits, while a user staring at silence talks over the agent.

UsageUnit.description: What a provider bills by. Singular, because a price is stated per one of it.

LayerMs.description: One layer of a turn's latency in milliseconds, as the worker measured it. Absent when the worker did not measure that layer for the turn, never zero in its place.

configHash.description: Ties this session to the exact resolved config it ran under, which is what makes it explainable afterwards.

SessionSignalPayload.description: The consumer-defined passthrough. Its data is open by design: this is the extension point that stops a consumer forking when they need to carry something the platform has no opinion about.

relayed.description: Whether media is going through a TURN relay rather than a direct path. Expect 10-20% of connections to relay, higher on mobile. Reported per connection because relay bandwidth is metered per tenant and doubles as a diagnostic: a rising relay share means the consumer's network changed, not that the platform did.

downtimeMs.description: Mobile clients drop constantly, so reconnection is the SDK's job rather than the consumer's. This is how long the gap actually was.

pool.description: Which worker pool took the job. Recorded per session so a second pool can be introduced and observed without guessing which sessions it served.

WakeSource.description: How a dormant agent was woken: name, somebody said its name; manual, somebody pressed a wake control, which the agent treats as that person calling it.

AgentStateChangedPayload.description: The single most important event for user experience. A consumer renders this directly, so it is typed rather than left for them to discover at runtime. An agent that waits to be called by name also says whether it is dormant, and when awake who woke it, as an opaque participant id and never a name or what they said, so the event stays safe to log. Sent again, with the same state and no previousState, when only that changes.

dormant.description: Present only when the session's addressing mode waits to be called. True: the agent hears the call but answers nobody until its name is said.

SpeakerKind.description: Who spoke a line: human, a participant who joined with a token the control plane minted; agent, the session's AI agent, whose identity the media server assigns and which is therefore never a participant id.

Speaker.description: Who said it, as an opaque participant id and never a name. A human line always names the participant; an agent line never does.

TranscriptSource.description: The recognizer that produced the text. A session that fell back mid-call has lines from two providers, so this is per line rather than per transcript.

CaptionSegmentPayload.description: One caption while it is being spoken: transcript.partial while the recognizer (or, for the agent, its speech) is still going, the whole segment so far each time; transcript.final once, when it settles. This is the realtime pass and never the record: it is not stored, and a consumer must not present it as the transcript of the call. It carries what somebody said, which error messages and logs never may. It is allowed here because captions are the point of the event and the session's transcription consent covers them: it is published only while transcription is live, to the call's own participants over its data channel (encrypted with the media under end-to-end encryption), and never logged, because the worker logs an event's type and sequence and never its payload.

segmentId.description: Opaque and minted by the worker. Every partial of a segment and the final that settles it share it, so a consumer replaces rather than appends.

source.description: The recognizer. Absent on the agent's own lines, whose text is the reply it spoke rather than anything recognised.

TranscriptLine.description: One line of a transcript, from one speaker's own recorded track, so the attribution is the recording's rather than a guess. startMs and endMs count from the start of that recording, whose start time the provenance states.

TranscriptVersionPayload.description: One version of a session's transcript of record, and the whole of it: the batch pass hands it to the control plane as this event, and the control plane checks its hash, numbers it and stores it. A re-run is a new version and never overwrites one, because the recorded audio is the source of truth and a transcript is derived from it. It carries what people said, like the caption payload, and is never logged.

transcriptHash.description: Hex SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 serialization of this payload with transcriptHash itself omitted: the scheme configHash uses, so an exported transcript can be re-hashed by whoever receives it.

pass.description: Which pass made it. Only the batch pass after the call makes a transcript of record; captions are never stored as one.

provenance.description: How it was made, enough to explain it or make it again.

configHash.description: The session's resolved config, which pins the provider and model and states the consent the transcription ran under.

recordings.description: Every recorded track the transcript was made from, and whose it is.

verbatim.description: Word for word, fillers, repetitions and spoken numbers as said.

clean.description: The same audio transcribed for reading: punctuated, numbers written as numbers, fillers dropped. Made by a separate pass over the audio, so its lines need not align one to one with the verbatim lines.

AgentTurnMetricsPayload.description: Where one agent turn's latency went, layer by layer, measured inside the worker. The user-side layers come from the user's message that the reply answers, so a turn the agent opened itself (a greeting) carries none of them. A consumer compares replyGapMs with the gap it heard itself; the difference is the network and playout on its side.

turn.description: The agent's turn within the session, counted from 0.

endpointMs.description: From the last voiced audio of the user's the worker received to the speech-to-text provider releasing end of speech: the provider's silence window and its wait for the final transcript. The framework starts every other user layer at that release, so none of them contains this.

endOfTurnDelayMs.description: From the end of the user's speech to the decision that their turn ended.

transcriptionDelayMs.description: From the end of the user's speech to the final transcript.

llmNodeTtfsMs.description: LLM time to the first sentence handed to TTS.

ttsNodeTtfbMs.description: TTS time to first audio byte.

playbackLatencyMs.description: From the first audio frame forwarded to playback reported started.

e2eLatencyMs.description: From the end of the user's speech to the agent starting to speak, as the agent framework measures it: its end of speech is the provider's release, so endpointMs comes before it.

replyGapMs.description: From the last voiced audio of the user's the worker received to the agent starting to speak: endpointMs and everything after it, the reply gap as the worker sees it. A client's heard gap adds the network and playout on both sides.

serial.description: True when the turn went serial: its first sentence reached TTS more than 500 ms after the LLM's first token (llmNodeTtfsMs minus llmNodeTtftMs) although that sentence was under 80% of the reply, so the reply waited on more than its first sentence and its latency tracked the length of the reply. A reply that is mostly its first sentence is not serial however long that sentence took. Present only when both LLM layers were measured.

UsageItem.description: One provider, model and unit's consumption so far. An item the price table has no row for is unpriced and carries no cost, because a zero would read as free.

SessionUsagePayload.description: What the session has consumed and what it cost in INR. Sent after each agent turn as a running figure and once more when the session ends; the last one sent is the one to keep.

final.description: True for the figure taken when the session ended.

costInr.description: The sum of the priced items. A floor, not a total, while unpricedItems is above zero.
